provision_decisions.note: Wording is verbatim and unaffected by the 2022 amendment, but 31-2022 s.16(9)(b) deleted a proviso at the end of rule (16)(b) that was still in force in April 2019 and is absent from the consolidated corpus text, so the April 2019 paragraph cannot be read in full.

The excerpt stops at the opening words of paragraph (b) and omits sub-paragraphs (i) to (iii), which are the conditions that actually govern consent to a division into lots, so as quoted s 8(1) reads as an unconditional duty to consent; the excerpt should be extended before the answer relies on it.

The excerpt is verbatim but begins mid-sentence and drops the subject ('An instrument executed or made on or after the 1st day of January, 1864 ... shall'), so it does not stand as a proposition on its own; the priority point it is cited for is correct.

Section 42 confers a right, subject to the prescribed regulations, to search and to obtain certified copies or extracts; it imposes no duty on a notary. The duty to obtain a certified extract of the folio was created by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022, s 16(10)(a), inserting rule (17)(b)(i), and did not exist in April 2019.

Rule (33) is triggered when a deed is executed or acknowledged before a notary, so on its terms it is a duty at execution rather than before drafting; it supports calling for the title deeds at the instruction stage only by inference.

The quoted words of s 2(1) were in force in April 2019, but the temporal note is wrong on the amending Acts: the corpus records no amendment event on 38-2014/s2, and Act No. 3 of 2017 inserted s 5A while Act No. 21 of 2018 amended ss 3 and 5A.

Section 13 governs the admissibility of a plan in evidence; it does not require a survey to be made. It supports the survey step only indirectly, and the requirement to define a divided share by its own boundaries and extent comes from Notaries Ordinance s 31 rule (16)(b), not from the Survey Act.

The quoted paragraph (a) concerns policies of insurance. The limb that carries the claim is paragraph (e), 'in all other cases, by the person drawing, making or executing such instrument', which is not in the excerpt.

added_provisions.reason: Land Reform Law s 66 defines 'agriculture' to include the growing of industrial crops and 'agricultural land' as land used or capable of being used for agriculture. The map applied the s 3(1) ceiling to a rubber block without citing anything that makes rubber land agricultural land, so the ceiling limb (CL-M093-Q01-010 and CL-M093-Q01-015) rested on an uncited premise. Added as supporting, with a verbatim excerpt confirmed by check, and a defines edge from PROV-M093-019.

question_decisions.note: The statutory backbone holds and the question does not depend on case law or Roman-Dutch doctrine, so authority_requirement stays statute_only and the question is not reserved. It is downgraded because three claims and the gold prose carry steps that no cited provision imposes as at April 2019: obtaining a certified extract of the folio (a duty created by 31-2022 s 16(10)(a), not law in 2019), requiring the registered 2016 bond to be discharged before drafting, and having the blocking out plan approved before drafting. The verifier may not rewrite the gold answer, so a lawyer must adjudicate.

disagreements.researcher_position: The notary should cause the search under s 31 rule (17)(a) and obtain a certified extract of the relevant folio, citing Registration of Documents Ordinance s 42.
disagreements.verifier_position: In April 2019 s 42 conferred only a right, subject to prescribed regulations, for an interested person or his agent to search and to obtain certified copies or extracts. The obligation on a notary to obtain a certified extract of the folio containing the last entry was created by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s 16(10)(a), inserting rule (17)(b)(i). Presenting the extract as a required step states the post-2022 position.

disagreements.researcher_position: Because the 2016 bond is registered and takes priority under Registration of Documents Ordinance s 7(1), the notary must require its discharge, or a release of the fifteen acres, before the deed is drawn.
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 7(1) fixes priority between instruments; it imposes no duty on a notary, and no other cited provision requires him to insist on discharge or release before drafting. The step is sound conveyancing practice but it is not carried by the map's statutory citations.

disagreements.researcher_position: The pre-drafting steps include having the fifteen-acre block surveyed and the blocking out plan approved.
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 23A(1) only forbids an officer of a local authority to approve a blocking out plan of such an estate without the Board's certificate under s 14. It does not require approval of the plan before the deed is drafted, and the local-authority approval machinery is outside the corpus. The survey is required in substance by rule (16)(b), not by Survey Act s 13, which is an admissibility rule.

unsupported_claims: CL-M093-Q01-008: reads Survey Act s 13 as requiring a survey plan. Section 13 governs only whether a plan is receivable in evidence; the requirement to define a divided share by its own boundaries and extent comes from Notaries Ordinance s 31 rule (16)(b).

CL-M093-Q01-013: the limb requiring the notary to insist that the 2016 bond be discharged or the block released before drafting is not carried by any cited provision, and the certified extract limb states the post-2022 duty.
CL-M093-Q01-018: the conclusion lists obtaining a certified extract and having the blocking out plan approved among the pre-drafting steps; neither is imposed by a cited provision as at April 2019.
temporal_issues: Notaries Ordinance s 31 rule (17): the corpus carries the paragraph (b) substituted by 31-2022 s 16(10)(a). The paragraph (b) actually in force in April 2019 is not in the corpus, and the answer's certified-extract step tracks the replacement text.

Notaries Ordinance s 31 rule (16)(b): the proviso deleted by 31-2022 s 16(9)(b) was in force in April 2019 and is absent from the corpus, so the April 2019 paragraph cannot be read in full. The quoted sentences are unaffected.

PROV-M093-017 (38-2014 s 2(1)): the temporal note attributes the April 2019 text to Acts No. 3 of 2017 and No. 21 of 2018. Neither amends s 2; 3-2017 inserted s 5A and 21-2018 amended ss 3 and 5A. The quoted words were nevertheless in force in April 2019.
PROV-M093-022 (7-1840 s 2): the corpus text is post-2024, and only the opening words, unchanged since 1840, are quoted. Accepted, and nothing in the answer turns on the later wording.
1-1907 s 38A (notary to explain the true nature of the transaction) was inserted by 6-2024 s 4 and was correctly excluded from the map.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Land Reform Law s 66 definitions of 'agriculture' and 'agricultural land' were missing; added as PROV-M093-901.

Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act s 8(1): the excerpt omits sub-paragraphs (i) to (iii) of paragraph (b), which are the conditions on which consent to a division into lots is granted, so as quoted it reads as an unconditional duty to consent.

Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act s 6: the excerpt quotes paragraph (a) on policies of insurance; the limb that supports the claim is paragraph (e), 'in all other cases, by the person drawing, making or executing such instrument'.
Registration of Documents Ordinance s 7(1): the excerpt begins mid-sentence and omits the subject of the sentence.
Notaries Ordinance s 32(1) disapplies rule (16) as to boundaries for five classes of instrument; none of them covers this deed, so it is not a live exception here. Checked, not added.

The Prescription Ordinance (No. 22 of 1871) is in the corpus and bears on how far back title is traced. The answer expressly leaves the depth of the search to practice rather than asserting a period, which the verifier accepts, but a lawyer may wish it mentioned.
case_law_dependence: None. The answer cites no case and no Roman-Dutch doctrine. The one concession to practice, how far back title should be traced, is stated as such rather than asserted, so the question stays statute_only.
enrichment_issues: FACT-M093-Q01-003 says the estate 'stands registered as an estate for rubber control purposes'. That phrase is close to naming the Rubber Control Act, on which the s 25 definition turns. It is needed to make the definition determinate and it does not name an Act or a section, but a lawyer should confirm it is not too strong a pointer.

FACT-M093-Q01-003 and FACT-M093-Q01-004 are marked synthetic_decisive and each explains why it is needed. FACT-M093-Q01-006 (the undischarged bond) is also marked decisive and its reason is sound, but the step the answer draws from it is not statutory (see disagreements).

No added fact names a statute or a section number or states the conclusion. The counterfactual on FACT-M093-Q01-008 ('more than thirty-five acres') is arithmetically consistent with the fifty-acre ceiling and the fifteen-acre purchase.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: No duplicate provisions. Three entries share 1-1907/s31 and two share 2-1958/s25 and 38-2014/s25, but each carries a distinct subsection or defined term, which the corpus body structure justifies.
The enriched background does not disclose the answer: it states facts (extent, registration, divided block, encumbrance, price, existing holdings, place of signing) without saying which steps follow.

lawyer_questions: Does the pre-drafting duty stated in the gold answer overstate the April 2019 law by treating the certified extract of the folio as a required step, when that duty was only created by Notaries (Amendment) Act No. 31 of 2022 s 16(10)(a)? If so, should the answer be corrected or the question reserved until an as-at-2019 edition of the Notaries Ordinance is in the corpus?
Is the notary under any duty, as opposed to a practice obligation to his client, to require the discharge of a registered mortgage bond or a release of the block before he draws the deed?

Is the enrichment fact that the estate 'stands registered as an estate for rubber control purposes' an acceptable way to make the s 25 definition determinate, or does it point too directly at the Rubber Control Act?
Should the answer state a period for tracing title back beyond the registered folio, given that the statutes are silent and the corpus holds the Prescription Ordinance?
